Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · School & learning

mistake noun

also error, make a mistake, slip, spelling mistake, by mistake, by mistake (wrongly), slip of the tongue, commit an error, make an error

classical

Cic. Att. 6.1.18: sī secus est, commūne errātum est
Traupman 104: by mistake, perperam

errātum, errātī n.

noun, second declension

a mistake, an error

A mistake one has made, in a fact or in conduct. To make a mistake is errāre or peccāre (Traupman 155); by mistake, imprūdēns or perperam (Traupman 104).

Other words

  • mendum, mendī n. — a mistake in writing, a slip

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 2.7.5: Castriciānum mendum nōs corrigēmus; Cic. Verr. 2.2.104 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 27, 29, 30; Traupman 310

    The mistake in a written text, a copy or an account, and so in schoolwork: mendum admittere, to make one (Traupman 29). The feminine menda is the same word, used so after Augustus (Suet. Aug. 87, Lewis & Short).

  • error, errōris m. — error, being wrong

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Suet. Aug. 88.1: commūnis hominum error est; Traupman 155; Traupman 310

    Properly a wandering; then a going astray from the truth, a mistaken belief.

  • vitium, vitiī n. — a fault (in speech or writing)

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Quint. 1.5.1; Traupman 247: vitium facere, to make a mistake; Traupman 310

    A defect; in the grammarians the faults of speech, barbarisms and solecisms.

  • peccātum, peccātī n. — a fault, a slip

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Publ. P 62: Peccātum extenuat, quī celeriter corrigit.; Traupman 381

    A fault of any kind; in church Latin a sin (see sin).

  • lapsus linguae — a slip of the tongue

    also used · modern · Traupman 107: a slip of the tongue, lapsus linguae

    Lewis & Short has lapsus in the figurative sense “a failing, error” as rare but classical (Cic. Ac. 1.45), but not the phrase with linguae.

Examples

  • errāstī, Lupe, littera sed ūnā: nam quō tempore praedium dedistī, māllem tū mihi prandium dedissēs

    You made a mistake, Lupus, but only by one letter: when you gave me a farm (praedium), I’d rather you had given me lunch (prandium)Mart. 11.18.25–27

  • nēmō nostrum nōn peccat. hominēs sumus, nōn deī

    every one of us makes mistakes; we’re human, not godsPetr. 75.1

  • Castriciānum mendum nōs corrigēmus

    I’ll correct the mistake in Castricius’s accountCic. Att. 2.7.5

  • mendum admittere

    to make a mistake, commit an errorTraupman 310

See also correct, correct, fail, improve, sin, spelling.
